permit_used: Aufenthaltserlaubnis zur freiberuflichen Tätigkeit (freelance visa, § 21 Abs. 5 AufenthG)
digital_nomad_note: There is no separate DN visa (per se-legal, not re-checked). The route is Aufenthaltserlaubnis § 21 Abs. 5 AufenthG (freelance): the profession must be freiberuflich under § 18 EStG (LEA Berlin), project financing, licences if needed, for those over 45 - pension provision (Make it in Germany; the sample adult is 40 - not applicable). Economic interest under Abs. 1 is not required for freelance (text of the law 'abweichend von Absatz 1'), but LEA Berlin still mentions 'positive Auswirkungen'. Main risk: whether data analysis falls under 'freie Berufe' (§ 18 EStG) or is considered a Gewerbe - this was not checked; if Gewerbe, § 21 Abs. 1 with economic interest is needed.
self_employed_note: § 21 (1) for business: economic interest or regional need, financing (mth-partner); for freelancing § 21 (5) is simplified: expected positive effect and qualification.
real_estate_note: No residence permit route via real estate.
family_note: Family reunification requires a resident/citizen relative; the sample adult has none, there is no separate route for this situation.
student_note: Student residence permit: working days and remote work for a foreign employer not checked on official pages; not a path for the sample adult.
local_clients: The official pages (LEA Berlin, Make it in Germany, § 21 Abs. 5) do NOT require German clients and do not exclude foreign ones. LEA asks for Honorarverträge or >=2 Letters of intent 'with details of the cooperation' without specifying the client's country.
registration_needed: For a freelancer — registration with the tax office (Finanzamt) and insurance; details were not checked in open sources. Se-legal: tax residency, as a rule, after ~6 months of continuous residence → tax on worldwide income.
employer_risk: No official position of the BMF/tax authorities on PE of a foreign employer due to an employee's home office was found. Visaguard.berlin (blog): "the place where the work is performed, not the employer's country, determines German jurisdiction".
penalty: § 98 Abs. 3 Nr. 1 AufenthG — Ordnungswidrigkeit (fine) for Erwerbstätigkeit without the required permit (per the dejure.org summary to § 95; the amount of the fine was not verified); § 95 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 AufenthG — stay without the required title when under an obligation to leave: imprisonment up to 1 year or a fine. Visaguard (blog): a Blue Card/residence permit without the right to self-employment + work for clients may 'jeopardize residence permit' — recommends a permit under § 21 (6).
notes: Did not open because of the proxy limit: make-it-in-germany.com (freelance), auswaertiges-amt.de (FAQ on self-employment), visaright.eu and gesetze-im-internet.de (text of § 21) — did not see the official text of § 21 AufenthG, only law firms' summaries and the LEA Berlin page. The blog visaguard.berlin claims that even remote work for foreign clients from Germany requires a permit (§ 21 Abs. 6) — confirmed only by the blog. Chancenkarte (up to 20 h/week of work). | Opened: service.berlin.de (official), dejure.org (text of § 2 and § 21; not an official site, but a legislation database), make-it-in-germany.com (federal portal — official). Did not open: gesetze-im-internet.de/aufenthg_2004/__21.html (robots.txt fetch: ConnectTimeout — not 403, did not bypass again). Not checked: § 98 Abs. 3 Nr. 1 / § 95 (penalties) against the primary source, § 19c, Chancenkarte, the procedure of applying from Turkey, tax/social insurance, classification of data analysis as Freiberuf.
conditional_class_note: A separate freelancer residence permit is needed (§ 21 Abs. 5 AufenthG); official pages do not require German clients, the question of recognising data analysis as a "liberal profession" is open.

permit_used: None established: no digital nomad or remote-work residence permit found on official pages; the B/2 visitor visa (up to 3 months) is stated by consular pages to bar work in Israel
digital_nomad_note: No digital nomad or remote-work scheme appears on the Israeli consular visa pages opened (B/2 visitor, B/1 work, A/2 student; Israeli missions) or on the Tel Aviv municipality work-visa page, which lists the expert, short-term expert, Innovation Visa and BETA routes only. A complete official list of visa types could not be opened (the gov.il visa guide returned no content), so absence of a scheme is not established as n_a.
self_employed_note: Innovation Visa for a foreign technology entrepreneur: stay permit of up to two years to establish a venture within an approved supporting framework; the Innovation Authority recommends, the Population and Immigration Authority grants (Israel Innovation Authority). The Tel Aviv municipality page describes it as a pilot. Other self-employment routes were not found on official pages.
family_note: Spouses and minor children may join a holder of the long-term expert work visa, with permits requested before arrival (Tel Aviv municipality page). Family routes for other permits were not checked on official pages.
student_note: A/2 student visa: "Recipients of this visa are not permitted to work in Israel" (Israeli consular page). The pages do not say whether remote work for a foreign employer is covered by that bar.
local_clients: Not clarified on the official pages: no page addresses remote work for clients inside Israel; any work in Israel needs a B/1 work visa approved by the Population and Immigration Authority (Israeli consular pages).
registration_needed: Not clarified on the official pages opened: no statement on tax, National Insurance or business registration for a foreign remote worker. A law-firm article (not official) notes a rebuttable presumption of Israeli tax residency at 183 days or more in a calendar year.
employer_risk: Not clarified: the official pages do not address permanent-establishment or tax risk for a foreign employer of a remote worker in Israel.
penalty: Not clarified on official pages. The Entry into Israel Law, 5712-1952 (unofficial consolidation on a UN refugee-agency database, omits later amendments) provides imprisonment for one year for entering or residing in contravention of the law (s.12(1)), makes infringement of a visa or permit condition an offence (s.12(3)) and allows a deportation order (s.13). Whether remote work on a visitor visa is a breach of such a condition is not stated on the pages opened.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: Israeli consular visa pages (B/2 visitor visa, B/1 work visa, A/2 student visa; embassies and missions of Israel), the Tel Aviv municipality page on work visas for foreigners and the Israel Innovation Authority page on the Innovation Visa. Classification: unknown. The consular pages state that a B/2 holder "is not allowed to work in the State of Israel", and that the B/1 work visa is granted only with approval of the Population and Immigration Authority; none of the pages opened says whether remote work for a foreign employer or foreign clients falls under that bar, and no digital nomad scheme was found. A law-firm article describes this as a grey area with no published guidance by the authority (not an official source). Not found or not opened: the gov.il visa guide and the Population and Immigration Authority pages (returned no content), the official text of the current Entry into Israel Law and Regulations, Israel Tax Authority pages on residency. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).

permit_used: Visado y autorización de residencia para teletrabajo de carácter internacional (digital nomad visa, Ley 14/2013 art. 74 bis et seq., introduced by Ley 28/2022)
digital_nomad_note: Direct target of the programme. Conditions: a third-country national, adult; a diploma from a prestigious university/professional training or ≥3 years of experience; employment/commercial relations with a foreign company ≥3 months at the time of application; the company actually operates ≥1 year; income ≥200% SMI + family; insurance, clean criminal record. Visa up to 1 year (via consulate), residence permit up to 3 years with extension by 2 years; can be applied from Spain at the UGE-CE.
passive_income_note: Did not open the official text on the "non-lucrative" / passive income route (conditions not checked on official pages). The right to work remotely under this residence permit is not confirmed (under general rules such a title does not imply work) — do not use as a route for work.
self_employed_note: Cuenta propia (autónomo) and the startup visa exist (conditions not checked on official pages); for self-employed remote work for foreign clients the main route is the nomad visa. The official pages on cuenta propia were not opened.
real_estate_note: The golden visa for real estate was closed on 03.04.2025 (not checked on official pages); former holders renew on the old terms.
family_note: Family reunification requires a resident/citizen relative; the sample adult has none, there is no separate route for this situation.
student_note: Student residence permit: working hours not checked on official pages; the possibility of remote work for a foreign client was not separately verified. Not a route for the sample adult (goal — work).
local_clients: Officially (PRIE, FAQ UGE): for professional (self-employed) activity, working for Spanish companies is permitted if it is no more than 20% of all professional activity; an employee in Spain may work only for a company located outside Spain (FAQ, question 14: 'En España sólo puede trabajar para la empresa radicada fuera del territorio nacional').
registration_needed: UGE FAQ (Ministry of Labour/Inclusion): when working from Spain, alta in Social Security is mandatory; for the self-employed: 'El propio trabajador se deberá dar de alta en el régimen de trabajadores autónomos (RETA)'; for employees the employer must be registered in advance as a non-resident in Social Security. The alternative is 'importación del derecho desde el país de origen', only if there is an international social security agreement between Spain and the country of origin (the social security body issues a document on the basis of the agreement).
employer_risk: The official position of AEAT/the Ministry of Finance on the creation of a permanent establishment (PE) by a foreign employer because of a resident remote worker was not found. This is a separate question from immigration status; it is not discussed in the immigration documents (PRIE, UGE).
penalty: LO 4/2000 (Ley de Extranjería) art. 53.1.b: "encontrarse trabajando en España sin haber obtenido autorización de trabajo" — a serious violation; fine from 501 to 10,000 € (art. 55.1.b); expulsion instead of a fine is possible (art. 57). Text of the law per the mirror papelea.com (BOE did not open directly in the needed part).
notes: The conditions «the company has existed >1 year, contract ≥3 months, degree or 3+ years» match the Spanish consulate in Santiago de Chile and PRIE. The income threshold on official pages is set as 200% of SMI (the specific euro amount is not given in the open official texts; SMI changes annually). The BOE pages of Ley 14/2013/Ley 28/2022 opened via WebFetch only partially (preamble); the exact text of art. 74 bis is confirmed by the papelea.com mirror and FAQ/PRIE. The tax regime (Beckham/non-resident) was not researched. Important for the sample adult: ≥3 months of employment/contractual relations with a company that has existed for ≥1 year — confirmation is needed from each client. | Verbatim verification of article 74 bis against the BOE failed: WebFetch truncates the text to art. 20 (BOE-A-2013-10074) and art. 29 (LO 4/2000, BOE-A-2000-544) — art. 53/55/57 LO 4/2000 (fines) remain confirmed only by the papelea.com mirror. The definition (remote work for companies outside Spain, 20% limit for professional activity, >=3 months of relations, visa 1 year / residence permit 3 years) is confirmed by the official PRIE page; 200% SMI, 1 year of company activity and 3 months — by the page of the Spanish consulate in Santiago de Chile («Requisitos visado TEL»). | Source check: the source 'Consulate in Santiago de Chile' (Requisitos visado TEL) does not mention the 20% limit — the limit is confirmed by PRIE and the UGE FAQ, not by this page.

permit_used: No dedicated remote-work visa found. Official Home Affairs policy (advice released under FOI, 2025) covers remote work for an overseas or metropolitan employer under the regional provisional visas (subclasses 491 and 494, condition 8579) if the holder lives in a designated regional area and the pay and income tax are in Australia; Visitor visa (subclass 600) is subject to a 'no work in Australia' condition (8101)
digital_nomad_note: No digital nomad visa found. The Home Affairs visa listing page did not show the list (page content not rendered) and the Visitor 600 page showed only its meta description ('For tourists, business visitors or to visit family for 3, 6 or 12 months'), so the absence of a nomad route is not confirmed on an official page. Law firm commentary (Hannan Tew; IBA article) discusses only the Visitor visa and Working Holiday visas for remote workers.
self_employed_note: The Home Affairs page for the Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa, subclass 188, describes it in its meta description as a provisional visa for people with business skills who want to operate or invest in Australia; eligibility, conditions and work rights were not readable (Department of Home Affairs).
family_note: Student visa (subclass 500): 'Secondary visa holders are subject to a visa condition that limits them to 48 hours work per fortnight at any time' (Department of Home Affairs, FOI release); the archived Home Affairs page says family members generally can work up to 40 hours per fortnight, with no limit if the primary holder studies a masters or doctoral degree. Family routes for other visas were not checked.
student_note: Student visa (subclass 500): 'You can work up to 48 hours every two weeks while studying and unlimited hours during study breaks' (Study Australia, Austrade); no official page opened says whether work for an overseas employer counts towards the limit.
local_clients: Not clarified for residence permits. For the Visitor visa Business Visitor stream, Home Affairs policy restricts visitors 'from working for or supplying services to an organisation or person in Australia' (Department of Home Affairs, GenGuideH policy released under FOI in 2018).
registration_needed: Tax: a foreign resident declares income earned in Australia; a temporary resident generally declares only income derived in Australia and capital gains on taxable Australian property, and overseas employment or services income may need declaring in certain circumstances (Australian Taxation Office). Business or social security registration of a remote worker was not checked.
employer_risk: Not clarified in general. For the regional visas 491 and 494, Home Affairs policy requires that for an overseas-based employer 'remuneration is paid to the visa holder in Australia and income tax is payable in Australia'.
penalty: Not clarified: the Home Affairs pages with the wording of condition 8101 and the consequences of breach (help-text pages) are closed to automated reading (robots.txt) and the legislation text could not be opened.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: Department of Home Affairs (FOI releases of the visitor visa policy GenGuideH, the 2025 advice on condition 8579 for subclasses 491 and 494, and the student visa work-limit document; archived page on student work conditions; Business Innovation and Investment 188 page, meta description only), Study Australia (Austrade) and the Australian Taxation Office. Classification: conditional, effectively no for a person who wants to relocate on a route built for remote work, because no such route was found: the Visitor visa carries a 'must not engage in work in Australia' condition (8101), the Business Visitor stream bars working for or supplying services to a person or organisation in Australia, and the one official statement found that explicitly allows remote work for an overseas employer concerns holders of regional skilled provisional visas (491/494), which need nomination or sponsorship and points; the document is described as a proposed clarification of policy. Law firm commentary (Hannan Tew, IBA) says Home Affairs policy treats limited online work incidental to a holiday, for an overseas employer, as generally not a breach of condition 8101; the body of the 'Online work' section of the policy could not be opened on an official page (the FOI copy shows the heading only), so this is not confirmed. Home Affairs visa pages (immi.homeaffairs.gov.au), the legislation register and AustLII could not be read. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).
conditional_class_note: Remote work for an overseas employer is explicitly addressed only for regional skilled provisional visas (491/494) that require nomination or sponsorship and points, while the Visitor visa carries a no-work condition and no digital nomad route was found.

passive_income_note: Settlement permit - gainful employment excepted: for people who settle in Austria without gainful employment (e.g. pensioners, financially independent individuals); a quota place is required and regular monthly income must reach EUR 2,616.78 for a single person (as of 1 January 2026), EUR 4,128.24 for a married couple or partnership, plus EUR 403.76 per child (oesterreich.gv.at; migration.gv.at). The page title excludes gainful employment; whether remote work for a foreign employer counts as gainful employment is not stated.
self_employed_note: Temporary residence permit 'Self-Employed Person': the applicant must prove a contractual obligation to carry out a specified self-employed activity and may not plan to stay longer than the duration of this obligation (Work in Austria immigration guide). Red-White-Red Card has a start-up founder category (migration.gv.at); conditions were not opened.
family_note: Red-White-Red Card Plus for family members exists (migration.gv.at); its work rights were not checked on an official page.
student_note: Not checked on official pages; the student permit appears in the migration.gv.at list of titles.
local_clients: Not clarified on the official pages: none of the pages reviewed states whether a holder of the settlement permit excluding gainful employment may serve clients in Austria.
registration_needed: Not clarified on the official pages: tax and social security duties of a person working remotely for a foreign employer were not found on official pages.
employer_risk: Not clarified: the official pages reviewed do not address permanent-establishment risk for a foreign employer of a remote worker in Austria.
penalty: Not clarified: the penalty provisions for unauthorised employment (Ausländerbeschäftigungsgesetz) could not be opened on an official page.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: migration.gv.at (residence titles for third-country nationals; other forms of settlement), oesterreich.gv.at (settlement permit excluding gainful employment), Work in Austria immigration guide (temporary employment), RIS (NAG; only the table of contents and definitions in section 2 opened). Work titles found on official pages are tied to employment or a contract in Austria. No prohibition of remote work for a foreign employer was found, so the earlier 'no' is not carried over. Not established: the text of NAG section 44 and of the definition of gainful activity (the RIS page showed only the heading), the Ausländerbeschäftigungsgesetz penalty section, any official digital nomad scheme (none found on migration.gv.at), tax and social security treatment. The start-up founder page on migration.gv.at returned a server error. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).

permit_used: Temporary residence permit issued by the State Migration Service on enumerated grounds (e.g. real estate worth at least AZN 100,000, term deposit, family, study); no remote-work or digital nomad permit in force
digital_nomad_note: A digital nomad visa subtype is not among the grounds for temporary residence on the State Migration Service pages (State Migration Service). It is planned: according to news agency reports of 20 August 2026 (APA, Report.az), the State Program for the Development of Tourism 2026-2030 provides for a digital nomad visa subtype, with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to prepare Migration Code amendments in 2027-2028; eligibility, income, stay length and fees are not published and the text of the State Program was not opened.
passive_income_note: Closest routes on the State Migration Service page are a fixed-term bank deposit or state/investment securities of at least AZN 100,000; no pension or passive income ground is listed, and the right to work remotely on these grounds is not stated (State Migration Service).
self_employed_note: Temporary residence on the entrepreneurship ground requires an employing business in the country: labour contracts with at least 5 persons full-time (or 10 part-time), with at least 80 percent of workers citizens of Azerbaijan (State Migration Service). This is a route for a local business, not for a freelancer serving foreign clients.
real_estate_note: Temporary residence permit is available for owners of real estate worth at least 100,000 manats (State Migration Service, page 'Temporary residence'); the 2023 amendments raised the threshold for permanent residence to AZN 200,000 (State Migration Service news of 16 May 2023). The right to work remotely for a foreign employer on this permit is not stated; paid work in the country requires a work permit.
family_note: Family membership with a foreigner or stateless person residing in Azerbaijan is a ground for temporary residence (State Migration Service). Work requires a work permit; the exemption list includes spouses of Azerbaijani citizens registered at their residence (State Migration Service work guide).
student_note: Full-time study at higher education institutions, technical schools or secondary schools is a ground for temporary residence (State Migration Service); remote work on a student permit is not addressed.
local_clients: Not clarified on the official pages: the work guide covers employment through Azerbaijani employers and branches or representative offices of foreign companies and says nothing about a foreigner working remotely for a foreign employer or serving local clients.
registration_needed: Not clarified for remote work. Foreigners must register their place of residence and re-register after moving (the Code of Administrative Offences fines failure to register, State Migration Service). Tax and social security duties of a remote worker are not addressed on the official pages.
employer_risk: Not clarified: the official pages opened do not address permanent-establishment or tax risk for a foreign employer of a remote worker in Azerbaijan.
penalty: Foreigners and stateless persons are fined AZN 300-400, with or without expulsion, for violating stay and residence rules, including paid labour without a required work permit (State Migration Service, Code of Administrative Offences summary). Employers face fines for engaging a foreigner without a work permit; older State Migration Service news items give AZN 3,000-5,000 for officials and AZN 30,000-35,000 for legal entities, with article numbers and dates that differ between items, so the current amounts are not established.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: State Migration Service of Azerbaijan (temporary residence page, work-permit guide last updated 20.01.2023, general work-permit page, news of 16 May 2023 on migration law amendments, liability pages). Classification: unknown. No official page states that a foreigner living in Azerbaijan may or may not work remotely for a foreign employer; the work guide says 'Concluding labour contract with foreigners without obtaining a work permit is prohibited' and covers employment by entities in Azerbaijan, so the question for a remote worker with no local employer is not addressed. The old threshold discrepancy is resolved: the State Migration Service states AZN 100,000 for temporary residence by real estate (the earlier figure of USD 60,000 came from a third-party source). A digital nomad visa is reported as planned (media reports of 20 August 2026) but not open and not defined. Not established: the text of the State Program for Tourism Development 2026-2030, the full Migration Code (e-qanun) and the e-visa purposes list were not opened; the migration.gov.az page on temporary residence in full wording was read only in summary. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).

permit_used: A residence permit as a sole proprietor is needed only if one opens a sole proprietorship and obtains the status. The new rules from 01.11.2026 mainly affect residence permits, not the right of EAEU citizens.
digital_nomad_note: There is no special digital nomad visa in Armenia; remote workers for a foreign employer usually get a residence permit as a sole proprietor (armenian-lawyer.com, overview of rules from 01.11.2026).
self_employed_note: armenian-lawyer.com (law firm): "Your work doesn't need to be connected to Armenia. You can serve international clients while benefiting from Armenian business registration"; the residence permit requires a sole proprietor certificate and confirmation of tax payments. Tax regimes: micro-business 0% at turnover up to 24 million AMD (≈$62,000), turnover tax 5% and others. From 01.11.2026: 1 million AMD in an account in Armenia or turnover ≥1 million AMD in the 60 days before filing; if no tax is accrued within 180 days after obtaining the status, the residence permit may be annulled; quotas on statuses by type; notification if the 183 days are not spent.
real_estate_note: Rental/registration at the place of residence: right to reside until the passport expires (not checked on official pages); right to work for EAEU citizens — without a permit (art. 97 of the EAEU Treaty, per a law firm).
family_note: The sample adult has no Armenian relatives.
student_note: Student residence permit: not verified.
local_clients: Yes: a sole proprietor in Armenia can work with both local and foreign clients (armenian-lawyer.com). EAEU citizens work on the same terms as Armenian citizens, without a work permit.
registration_needed: Not clarified on the official pages.
employer_risk: Not clarified: Did not find Armenia's official position on the PE of a foreign client because of a sole-proprietor worker.
penalty: For sole proprietors (IE): the residence permit can be revoked if no tax is paid for 180 days and if absent from Armenia for 183 days (new rules from 01.11.2026, armenian-lawyer.com). Penalties for working without a right are not relevant to EAEU citizens (no permit needed). Articles/amounts not found.
notes: The discrepancy over the date of the law has been resolved by law firms: adopted 20.01.2026, enters into force 01.11.2026 (EY Armenia, armenian-lawyer, Schneider; applications filed before that date are processed under the old rules). Clarification on the author's doubt: Schneider Group — "Foreign nationals entitled to work by virtue of Armenia's international treaties, including nationals of EAEU member states, remain exempt"; the categories that lost the exemption (founders/directors, and others) do not concern EAEU citizens. Thresholds: sole proprietor (IE) — AMD 1 million on the account or turnover of AMD 1 million over 60 days (armenian-lawyer, Schneider); EY: AMD 2 million of charter capital or 1 million for an IE. Temporary status — up to 1 year with no extension mechanism (Schneider); quotas by type; refusal when the quota is exhausted. The certificate of legal residence for EAEU citizens after 01.11.2026 is paid: armenian-lawyer — AMD 35,950; the author's note (AMD 30,000 from 2027, workpermit.am) — discrepancy, not verified. Official source (migration/arlis/e-gov, text of the law, EAEU Treaty) NOT found: only law firms remained accessible. WebSearch limit exhausted.

permit_used: Professional card (self-employment, regional decision) + D visa → residence card
digital_nomad_note: There is no separate digital nomad visa in Belgium (expat.com: two paths — single permit with a Belgian employer or professional card + D visa).
self_employed_note: Professional card (the region decides on the 'usefulness of the project'; Brussels: business plan <=20 pages, €140 + €90/year, term 2 years->up to 5 years; Ministry of Foreign Affairs: then D visa €180 + €242). Financial threshold: expat.com (blog) gives 110% of the subsistence minimum = €26,086.66 (03.2026) specifically for Flanders. Did not find an official threshold. For remote work for foreign clients there is no official definition.
family_note: Family reunification requires a resident/citizen relative; the sample adult has none, there is no separate route for this situation.
student_note: Study (conditions not checked on official pages); right to remote work not verified separately.
local_clients: The official pages do not say; the professional card is oriented towards business in Belgium and an assessment of benefit to the region (clients in Belgium are implied).
registration_needed: The professional card is obtained on site at the “company counter” (guichet d'entreprise) indicated in the application (dofi.ibz.be).
employer_risk: expat.com (blog): income from a foreign employer/clients is not automatically exempt from Belgian tax; the official position of the Belgian tax authority on PE not found.
penalty: Not clarified (sanctions are not listed on the open dofi/region pages).
notes: Regionality: the professional card is decided by three regions (Brussels, Flanders, Wallonia) — only Brussels was researched. The income threshold from expat.com (≈€26,087, 2026) is not confirmed on an official page — did not find the current official threshold. Official pages do not define remote work for foreign clients, so conditional is a grey area/estimate. Key risk: the regional commission assesses the benefit of the project for the region, which is weaker for a purely foreign clientele. | Only Brussels was researched (official page); the Flanders page (vlaio.be/en/professional-card — URL guessed) returned 404, Wallonia did not open. The expat.com blog is confirmed verbatim: 'Belgium has no digital nomad visa'; 'No short-stay category expressly authorizes ongoing remote work for a foreign employer or foreign clients'; 'no separate remote worker category'; tax on income from foreign clients is not removed automatically. permit_used: Standard Visitor (Appendix Visitor: Permitted Activities, PA 4(h)): activities relating to overseas employment may be done remotely from within the UK if this is not the primary purpose of the visit; stay up to 6 months. For longer residence the question depends on a work-rights permit (for example Global Talent, which permits self-employment)
digital_nomad_note: The GOV.UK list of work visas names no digital nomad or remote worker visa (GOV.UK, Work visas page). The only remote-work rule found is the Standard Visitor activity in PA 4(h).
passive_income_note: The GOV.UK list of work visas contains no retirement or passive income route; the Investor visa (Tier 1) is listed as closed to new applicants (GOV.UK, Work visas page).
self_employed_note: Global Talent permission allows work including self-employment, except as a professional sportsperson (Immigration Rules, Appendix Global Talent, GT 7.3(b)); the route needs an endorsement or prestigious prize and is limited to leaders or potential leaders in academia or research, arts and culture, or digital technology (GOV.UK, Global Talent). The Innovator Founder visa also exists (GOV.UK, Work visas page); its conditions were not checked.
real_estate_note: No route based on property ownership appears in the GOV.UK list of work visas (GOV.UK, Work visas page); the page covers work routes only, family and study routes were not listed there.
family_note: Dependent partners and children of Global Talent holders may work, except as a professional sportsperson or sports coach (Appendix Global Talent, GT 24.3(b)). The GOV.UK partner/spouse page does not state work rights.
student_note: Student visa: work depends on the course and term time; being self-employed is listed among the things a student cannot do (GOV.UK, Student visa: work). Work for an overseas employer is not addressed on that page.
local_clients: Visitors may not do other paid or unpaid work in the UK without a work visa; work for a UK customer must be done outside the UK (Appendix Visitor: Permitted Activities, PA 4(g); GOV.UK, Visit on business). Global Talent permission places no client restriction in GT 7.3(b).
registration_needed: Not clarified for the visitor route. A person who is UK resident for tax normally pays UK tax on all income, including foreign income; residence turns on days spent in the UK and the Statutory Residence Test (GOV.UK, Tax on foreign income: residence).
employer_risk: Not clarified: the official pages reviewed do not address permanent-establishment or payroll risk for a foreign employer of a remote worker in the UK.
penalty: Working while disqualified by immigration status is a criminal offence for a person who knows or has reasonable cause to believe it: up to 51 weeks' imprisonment and/or a fine in England and Wales, up to 6 months and/or a fine in Scotland and Northern Ireland (Immigration Act 1971, s. 24B). Employer civil penalty amounts were not opened on an official page.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: GOV.UK (Appendix Visitor: Permitted Activities; Standard Visitor, Visit on business; Work visas; Global Talent; Appendix Global Talent; Student visa work; Tax on foreign income residence), legislation.gov.uk (Immigration Act 1971, s. 24B). Classification: conditional, effectively no for residence-based remote work. Remote work for an overseas employer is expressly allowed to a Standard Visitor only as a non-primary purpose of a visit of up to 6 months; the GOV.UK work-visa list has no digital nomad or remote-worker permit. A permit with general work rights (for example Global Talent) lets the holder work, including self-employed, but admission to it depends on endorsement. Not established: whether the Skilled Worker, Innovator Founder and family routes permit work for an overseas employer in addition to the sponsored role; the GOV.UK Visit on business page does not mention remote work; employer civil penalty page (GOV.UK) could not be opened. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).
conditional_class_note: Remote work for an overseas employer is formally allowed for Standard Visitors (up to 6 months, not the primary purpose of the visit), but no residence permit exists for remote work and the permits with general work rights need an employer sponsor, an endorsement or a start-up route.

permit_used: A separate residence permit or work permit for services to foreign clients is not needed PROVIDED that all clients are non-residents and the services relate to their activity outside Georgia: art. 1(4) of the law on labour migration (version of 25.06.2026, matsne) takes such services outside the scope of the law. The exception is formulated by the nature of the activity, not by sole proprietor status; neither the law nor the explanations found (KPMG, AmCham, ibccs, Gegidze) say anything separately about a sole proprietor with Small Business Status, and Gegidze states directly that a foreign sole proprietor with Georgian clients remains under the law - hence conditional.
digital_nomad_note: Remotely from Georgia programme (visa/visa-free stay up to 12 months, income $2,000/month, no extension; armenian-lawyer.com — law firm). Separate IT-nomad residence permit: IT experience 2+ years and $25,000/year (pbservices) — a data analyst may not qualify. Since April 2026 these requirements are not mandatory for remote work for foreign clients (see self_employed).
self_employed_note: Parliament of Georgia, 15.04.2026: the law does not apply to someone who provides services to a non-resident if «such activities are related to operations carried out outside the territory of Georgia». Gegidze (law firm): «You can live in Tbilisi full-time and still be fully exempt, provided your clients are non-Georgian»; a foreign sole proprietor selling services to Georgian clients in Georgia still falls under the regime. Tax: Small Business Status — 1% of turnover (limit GEL 500,000), income received physically in Georgia is considered Georgian (Gegidze, armenian-lawyer — law firms). Check 04.10.2026: the exception of art. 1(4) — «services to a non-resident connected with activity outside Georgia» (parliament.ge) / «provided that such labor activities or services are directly connected to the non-resident employer carrying out its operations outside Georgia» (AmCham) — operates by the type of work and does not mention a sole proprietor or Small Business Status. Condition for the applicant: all clients are foreign legal entities/persons, the work is connected with their activity outside Georgia; with a mixed clientele Gegidze considers the Georgian part "fact-specific" (small and incidental — low risk, substantial — legal advice is needed). A Georgian client or the client's activity in Georgia takes one out of the exception: then the right to engage in labour activity is needed (fine GEL 2,000). Art. 13^9 of the law — short-term professional activity (up to 4 months per calendar year), does not apply to permanent remote work. KPMG Flash Alert 2026-117 describes the rules from 01.03.2026 up to the April amendment and does not mention the exception for non-residents; self-employed persons must obtain the right to labour activity through the portal.
real_estate_note: Residence permit via real estate (conditions not checked on official pages) — the right to work under this programme was not separately verified; for remote work, non-residents do not need a work permit (amendments 04.2026).
family_note: The sample adult has no relatives who are Georgian citizens.
student_note: Student residence permit: not verified.
local_clients: A work permit (self-employed) is needed via labourmigration.moh.gov.ge: per Gegidze, a foreign sole proprietor (IE) selling services to Georgian clients in Georgia remains under the regime. Data on turnover thresholds are contradictory (pbservices: GEL 50,000 turnover and income ≥5 subsistence minimums; expathub: GEL 50,000 per foreign worker) — currency not confirmed.
registration_needed: A sole proprietor is registered at the House of Justice and the Revenue Service (RS); with Small Business Status — 1% of turnover, monthly return. Tax residency — 183+ days.
employer_risk: Not clarified. Did not find an official position on the PE of a foreign client because of a sole-proprietor worker in Georgia.
penalty: For illegal labour activity: a fine of GEL 2,000 on the employer and on the employee (for each), for a repeat offence — doubled (GEL 4,000), then GEL 12,000 (mkdlaw, Revera — law firms; Did not open the text of the law on matsne.gov.ge). Work in a 'remote without entry' mode is an exception; Revera: «Entering Georgia while working remotely may result in the work permit being revoked» (this concerns remote work for a local employer).
notes: Officially confirmed (parliament.ge, 15.04.2026, 75 votes): the law does not apply to those who «provides services to a non-resident entity, where such activities are related to operations carried out outside the territory of Georgia», and to remote work for a local employer without entering the country. The exact text is quoted by AmCham Georgia: «...provided that such labor activities or services are directly connected to the non-resident employer carrying out its operations outside Georgia». The condition is critical: clients are non-residents with activity outside Georgia. The date of entry into force of the amendment is not stated on parliament.ge (Gegidze: effective immediately, 16.04.2026; not officially confirmed). Earlier (before April 2026) the official page of the Georgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (norway.mfa.gov.ge, rules from 01.03.2026) required the right to work for any paid work, including remote — this is outdated. EY Georgia: from 01.03.2026 D1/permit is not needed when working fully remotely without entering the country. The text on matsne.gov.ge and labourmigration.moh.gov.ge did not open. 404); 365 consecutive days»). Taxes: income from work physically performed in Georgia is Georgian-source (Gegidze, not re-verified).
conditional_class_note: The law of 15.04.2026 removes from the work permit requirement services to non-residents if the client's activity is conducted outside Georgia.

permit_used: Residence as a rentier under Law 171-07 (stable income from abroad of at least US$2,000 per month) or ordinary temporary residence RT-9 (proof of economic solvency); the law lets residents carry out remunerated activity, but no official page addresses remote work for a foreign employer
digital_nomad_note: The residence services page of the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) lists 15 residence services (RT-9, RT-3, RT-4, investor, rentier, pensioner and others) and none is a digital nomad or remote-work residence; the DGM resolutions page lists no resolution on digital nomads (DGM). An opinion piece in Dominican Today (June 2026) asks the president to create such a visa, which indicates none exists.
passive_income_note: Rentier residence is for a beneficiary of a monthly or permanent income of at least US$2,000 from a company or agency of foreign origin; Law 171-07 art. 3 sets US$2,000 for rentiers and US$1,500 for pensioners, plus US$250 per dependent, and art. 6 requires stable income from abroad for not less than five years (DGM, Law 171-07). The DGM pensioner page states that income earned by wages does not apply.
self_employed_note: Not checked on official pages as a stand-alone route. The DGM lists an investor residence ("exclusively to make investments") and a residence for management or technical staff of a foreign company; their requirements were not opened. Law 285-04 art. 99 allows temporary residents to carry out remunerated or lucrative activities during the authorised stay (DGM).
real_estate_note: Not checked on official pages as a residence route; the DGM lists investment residence, requirements not opened. Law 171-07 art. 13 gives tax reductions on first-property transfers to rentiers and pensioners (DGM), which is not a residence route.
family_note: Law 171-07 art. 3 allows dependents to apply with the rentier or pensioner (US$250 per month extra income per dependent), and the pensioner page lists spouse and minor children, or children over 18 who depend on the holder because of study or disability (DGM). Right of dependents to work was not stated on the pages opened. The DGM also lists a dependent temporary residence (RT-7).
student_note: DGM resolution DGM-02-2022 regulates a student subcategory of RT-9 (proof of funds by self, family or scholarship) and does not address whether holders may work (DGM).
local_clients: Not clarified on the official pages: Law 285-04 art. 99 lets temporary residents carry out remunerated or lucrative activities during the authorised stay without distinguishing local or foreign clients, while art. 101 penalises engaging in an activity different from the one stated in the entry documents (DGM).
registration_needed: Residents must obtain, keep valid and carry the migration identity document (Law 285-04 art. 25) and notify the DGM of a change of address (art. 73). Law 171-07 art. 15 provides that rentiers and pensioners may take paid work and that the salary is subject to Dominican taxes (DGM); the declared qualifying income is exempt from income tax (art. 10). Tax registration steps with the tax authority were not opened: not clarified.
employer_risk: Not clarified: the official pages opened do not address permanent-establishment or tax risk for a foreign employer of a remote worker in the Dominican Republic.
penalty: Law 285-04 art. 56: a person who carries out labour activity without the proper card "será considerado como un extranjero ilegal, sujeto a deportación"; art. 101: foreigners staying illegally may not work, and that article also covers engaging in an activity different from that stated in the entry documents; art. 100: non-residents may not carry out remunerated or lucrative tasks of any nature. Employers: fines of three to ten minimum salaries per violation for temporary workers (art. 131) and five to thirty minimum salaries for employers of illegal foreigners (art. 132), as extracted from the DGM-hosted text; article numbering should be confirmed against the full law (DGM).
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: Dirección General de Migración (residence services page, rentier, pensioner, RT-9 and RT-3 service pages, resolutions page, Resolution DGM-02-2022), Law 285-04 (General Migration Law) and Law 171-07 (special incentives for pensioners and rentiers from foreign sources) as hosted by the DGM. Classification: conditional, works with a note. Law 285-04 art. 99 allows temporary residents to carry out remunerated or lucrative activities, art. 98 allows permanent residents any remunerated work, and Law 171-07 art. 15 states that pensioners and rentiers "podrán ocuparse de labores remuneradas" with the salary subject to Dominican taxes; art. 100 bars non-residents from remunerated tasks of any nature. No official page opened mentions remote work for a foreign employer or foreign clients, a nomad visa, or the tax treatment of foreign-source salary of a resident, so the application of these norms to remote work is not confirmed. The rentier permit requires stable income from abroad for five years (rents rather than salary), and the pensioner page excludes wages; RT-9 requires proof of solvency, and the RT-9 page lists a bank statement with a minimum balance of 300,000 pesos. The English-language DGM pages do not state a right to work for the rentier, pensioner or RT-9 permits. Not opened: tax authority (DGII) pages, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa pages, the investor residence page. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).
conditional_class_note: The law allows residents (including rentiers, with the salary taxed) to take remunerated work, but no official page addresses remote work for a foreign employer, and the rentier permit rests on passive income of at least US$2,000 per month from abroad rather than on a salary.

notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: Immigration Service Delivery (irishimmigration.ie: retirement page, immigration permission stamps page, work and living pages, work FAQ, STEP page and STEP guidelines of September 2023), Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment (employment permits page) and Citizens Information. Routes with a right to work exist (employment permit tied to an Irish employer, STEP for an own Irish-based business, Stamp 4 categories), but none allows employment by a foreign employer without an employment permit on the pages opened. registration_needed: Main applicants are automatically registered for tax with the Malta Tax and Customs Administration after receiving the Nomad Residence Card; income from authorised work is not taxable in the first 12 months from the later of the permit issue date or 1 January 2024, then taxed at 10%; other income is taxed at the ordinary rates; the permit does not grant tax residency; a foreign tax credit requires proof of at least 10% foreign tax by 31 March of the following year; the Agency must be notified of any change in employment status; address changes must be reported within 10 working days. The FAQ warns that tax obligations might arise under both foreign and Maltese law. Social security is not addressed on the official pages: not clarified.
employer_risk: Malta Tax and Customs Administration rules: the employer must not be resident in Malta and must not trade in Malta through a fixed place of business; 'Eligible applicants will not be subject to FSS payments' and the non-resident employer avoids the usual Maltese employment-related requirements provided it does not become resident for tax purposes in Malta. A move to a Malta-resident employer ends nomad status for tax purposes. Permanent-establishment risk beyond this is not clarified on the official pages.
penalty: The Agency 'reserves the right to revoke the Nomad Residence Permit should it become aware of such activity' (work for Maltese companies); failure to report an address change may also lead to revocation; the Agency's decision is final with no appeal (FAQ v.12). Fines or criminal sanctions for unauthorised work were not found on the official pages: not clarified.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: Residency Malta Agency (Nomad Residence Permit home page, Nomad eligibility page, Nomad FAQ v.12 PDF), Malta Tax and Customs Administration (Nomad guidelines PDF, file dated 12-03-2026) and the Identita expatriates portal. The permit exists specifically to let holders keep working for an employer or clients abroad while living in Malta, but only for third-country nationals (EU, EEA and Swiss nationals are excluded; certain nationalities are currently not eligible per the FAQ), with gross income of at least EUR 42,000 per year, and with no Maltese employer or Maltese-based clients. The Residency Malta main site and the Identita permit-type subpages could not be opened. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).

permit_used: A residence permit that gives the right to work in Norway (the Norwegian Directorate of Immigration, UDI, states that remote work requires such a permit); no permit specific to remote work for a foreign employer or foreign clients is listed. digital_nomad_note: No digital nomad permit is named on the UDI remote-work page or on the UDI skilled-worker page; the full list of UDI work-immigration permit types could not be opened, so absence is not established (UDI).
self_employed_note: Residence permit as self-employed with a company in Norway: normally a sole proprietorship ("The business cannot be a limited company"), likely profit of at least NOK 310,070 per year before tax, residence in Norway and active part in running the business. The self-employed permit page does not mention foreign clients.
registration_needed: Not clarified for remote work for a foreign employer. The Norwegian Tax Administration page opened only states that a tax deduction card is needed to work in Norway and that a move to Norway must be reported; employer and social security duties for foreign employers are not addressed there (Skatteetaten).
employer_risk: Not clarified: the official pages reviewed do not address permanent-establishment, payroll or social security risk for a foreign employer of a worker resident in Norway.
penalty: Not clarified for the worker: the English text of section 108 of the Immigration Act (Penalties, as published by the Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority) penalises a person who with intent or gross negligence "makes use of a foreign national's labour" when the foreign national does not hold the required permit; the excerpt opened does not state a maximum fine or prison term and has no separate penalty for the foreign national's own unauthorised work.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: UDI (remote work page, skilled-worker page, self-employed with a company in Norway page, work-while-studying page), Skatteetaten (tax liability page) and the Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority (English text of Immigration Act section 108). Classification: conditional. UDI states that remote work (working for a Norwegian or foreign employer off-site, or running business activities in Norway or abroad) generally requires "a residence permit that gives you the right to work remotely in Norway", and that all foreigners working in Norway must have a residence permit. Visitors may do limited remote work for an employer or business abroad (checking and answering emails, calls, digital meetings) only if remote work is not the main purpose of the stay and the work does not create value in Norway; working for the employer in the home country while in Norway is generally not allowed. The permits UDI describes for work (skilled worker with a concrete job offer from a specific employer in Norway; sole proprietor with a company in Norway; employee on assignment from a foreign company with a contract with a Norwegian enterprise) are each tied to Norwegian activity, and the self-employed permit expressly excludes other work including remote work. No permit built for remote work for a foreign employer or foreign clients was found, so the verdict rests on the general rule that a permit with the right to work is required. Which other permits (for example family permits) carry an unrestricted right to work was not established on the pages opened; the UDI work-immigration overview and family-immigration rights pages could not be opened. UDI states that EU/EEA citizens are not covered by the permit requirement. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).
conditional_class_note: Formally a permit with the right to work covers remote work, but UDI names no permit for working remotely for a foreign employer or foreign clients, and the permits it describes are tied to Norwegian employers or businesses.

Dependant's Pass holders who own a business can apply for a Letter of Consent (ACRA).
family_note: Dependant's Pass is for spouses and children of Employment Pass or S Pass holders; ONE Pass and EntrePass holders can bring eligible family members, and a ONE Pass holder's spouse can apply to work on a Letter of Consent (MOM). A Dependant's Pass or Long-Term Visit Pass holder needs no work pass for overseas-based clients (MOM); work for Singapore-based employers needs a Letter of Consent or work pass (MOM).

Remote work for a foreign employer on a Student's Pass is not addressed on the pages opened, although the MOM answer on overseas-based employers is not limited to one pass type.
local_clients: No: a work pass is needed to work for or provide services to a Singapore-based organisation or client, and being self-employed does not change this; a Singapore-based organisation is one registered with ACRA (MOM, AskGov).
registration_needed: IRAS: income from work exercised in Singapore is taxable for foreigners; a non-resident working 60 days or less in a year is generally exempt, except directors, public entertainers and professionals such as consultants, trainers and coaches (IRAS). How this applies to a person who works for an overseas employer while living in Singapore is not addressed on the pages opened: not clarified. A foreigner who runs a business in Singapore must register it through a corporate service provider and have a local resident (ACRA).
employer_risk: MOM (AskGov): employers of record may not apply for work passes for foreigners who are based in Singapore while working for overseas companies, and doing so would be an offence; that answer also says a foreigner who will be based in Singapore for an extended period must be hired by their company on a regular work pass, or the company can use a representative office or a local company. This sits next to the MOM answer that an overseas-based employer needs no work pass; the two answers are not reconciled on the pages. Permanent-establishment and corporate tax risk is not addressed: not clarified.
penalty: Employing a foreign employee without a valid work pass: fine of S$5,000 to S$30,000, or imprisonment for up to 12 months, or both, higher for repeat offences (MOM, Employment of Foreign Manpower Act page). MOM states that working without a valid work pass is an offence for foreign students; the sanction for a worker is not stated on the pages opened. ICA: a visit pass holder "shall not engage in any form of employment (paid or unpaid), business, profession, or occupation in Singapore" while the pass is valid.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: Ministry of Manpower (FAQ on self-employed or overseas-employer work, passes-and-permits list, ONE Pass, EntrePass, Dependant's Pass, Long-Term Visit Pass, student work exemption, Employment of Foreign Manpower Act page), AskGov answers by MOM, ICA visit pass page, IRAS and ACRA. Classification: conditional. MOM's FAQ states that working for or providing services to an overseas-based organisation or client needs no work pass; this applies to someone who is physically in Singapore on a pass that allows stay (the AskGov question is framed around a stay pass such as the Dependant's Pass). Visit pass holders (tourist or social visit) are barred by ICA from employment, business or occupation in Singapore, and the official pages do not say whether remote work for an overseas employer is covered. Singapore has no pass for a remote worker as such, so a stay pass has to come from another basis (family, study, employment or business in Singapore). ONE Pass: fixed monthly salary of at least S$30,000 for 12 months, with an established company test (market capitalisation of at least US$500 million or annual revenue of at least US$200 million); under the second track the employer must be an established company based in Singapore; the pass allows concurrent work for multiple companies and runs up to 5 years. Not opened or not found: ICA page that states the work ban for tourists in full text, the Economic Development Board pages on investor routes, an official statement on tax treatment of an overseas-employed resident. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).
conditional_class_note: Formally no work pass is needed for overseas-based clients or employers once the person holds a pass that allows stay, but no pass exists for a remote worker as such, so residence has to come from family, study, or employment or business in Singapore.

permit_used: Digital Nomad Visa (DNV) issued by the Department of Foreign Affairs under Executive Order No. 86 of 24 April 2025: non-immigrant visa for foreigners working remotely for clients or employers situated outside the Philippines, valid up to 1 year
digital_nomad_note: Executive Order No. 86 authorises the DFA to issue DNVs to non-immigrant foreigners 'for the purpose of working remotely using digital technologies' 'whose clients or employers are situated outside the Philippines'; maximum stay 1 year (Executive Order No. 86, text as reproduced on lawphil.net). The Philippine embassy page lists the requirements: age 18+, proof of remote work using digital technology, proof of sufficient income generated outside the Philippines (no amount stated), no criminal record, health insurance valid for the DNV period, 'Must not be employed in the Philippines', and a national of a country that offers DNVs to Filipinos and where the Philippines has a Foreign Service Post, i.e. eligibility depends on reciprocity (DFA, Embassy in The Hague). The DFA guidelines, fees, income threshold, application steps and the list of eligible countries were not found on any official page opened.
passive_income_note: Special Resident Retiree's Visa (SRRV), issued by the Bureau of Immigration through the Philippine Retirement Authority: principal applicant must be 40 or older; visa deposit USD 15,000 to 50,000 for the Classic type depending on age and pension status (a lifetime pension of at least USD 800 per month for a single Classic pensioner); the page does not say whether holders may work, it states only that holders are exempt from 'Separate work/student visa or permits' (Philippine Retirement Authority).
self_employed_note: No official page opened states whether a DNV holder may run an own business; the Order requires that the holder 'Must not be employed in the Philippines'. A law firm review (Divina Law, 20 July 2026) says DNV holders cannot take local employment or operate a business; not confirmed on an official page. The Bureau of Immigration visa list also shows Treaty Trader or Treaty Investor (9D) and Special Visa for Employment Generation; their conditions were not checked.
real_estate_note: Not checked on official pages: no residence-by-property route was found on the Bureau of Immigration visa list (Permanent Resident Visa, Quota Visa, Temporary Resident Visa, Temporary Visitor Visa, Treaty Trader or Treaty Investor, Student Visa, Pre-arranged Employment Visa, special visas) but the conditions of each were not read.
family_note: Executive Order No. 86 contains no provisions on family members of DNV holders. SRRV: a legally married spouse and unmarried children under 21 can be included as dependents, USD 300 application fee each; a USD 15,000 additional deposit is required for each dependent beyond two (Philippine Retirement Authority).
student_note: The Bureau of Immigration lists a Student Visa (9F); its work conditions could not be opened (page returned an error), so whether a student may work remotely for a foreign employer is not established.
local_clients: Not clarified for serving clients inside the Philippines: the DNV is defined for foreigners 'whose clients or employers are situated outside the Philippines' and requires that the holder 'Must not be employed in the Philippines' (Executive Order No. 86; DFA Embassy page); no official page opened says anything about local clients as such.
registration_needed: Not clarified: Executive Order No. 86 contains no tax provisions and no social security rules; the Bureau of Internal Revenue appears only among the coordinating agencies. Tax residence and registration duties of a DNV holder were not found on official pages.
employer_risk: Not clarified: no official page opened addresses permanent-establishment or tax risk for a foreign employer of a remote worker in the Philippines.
penalty: Labor Code of the Philippines (Presidential Decree No. 442), Article 40: an alien seeking admission for employment, and an employer hiring an alien, must obtain an employment permit from the Department of Labor; Article 41: a non-resident alien who takes up employment in violation of the Title is punished under Articles 289 and 290 of the Labor Code and is subject to deportation after serving the sentence. The text of Articles 289 and 290 (fines, imprisonment) was not read. These articles are about employment in the Philippines; whether remote work for a foreign employer falls under them is not stated.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: Philippine Embassy in The Hague (DFA) digital nomad visa page, Bureau of Immigration visa list, Philippine e-Visa policy page, Philippine Retirement Authority SRRV page, Executive Order No. 86 (text reproduced on lawphil.net, a legal database, not a government site) and the Labor Code (also lawphil.net). Classification: conditional. An official order and an embassy page establish a visa for remote work for clients or employers outside the Philippines, with a reciprocity condition on nationality (the applicant's country must offer DNVs to Philippine nationals and host a Philippine Foreign Service Post). Not established: the DFA implementing guidelines (the Order asked for them within 30 days), the list of eligible countries, the income threshold, fees and whether applications are being accepted; a law firm review dated 20 July 2026 says the DFA has not published an official list of qualifying countries. The Bureau of Immigration site did not show a DNV in its visa list. Temporary visitor rules (e-Visa policy page): business visitors (9(a-1)) 'will not receive any compensation from a company/entity in the Philippines'; visa-free and e-Visa stays are not extendable and not convertible to other visa types, and the page does not say whether remote work is allowed on them. The DFA site, the DOLE alien employment permit FAQ and the Bureau of Immigration student visa page could not be opened. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).
conditional_class_note: The DNV exists in an executive order and on a Philippine embassy page and fits remote work for foreign clients or employers; eligibility depends on reciprocity (country list not published on the pages opened) and the implementing guidelines, income threshold and fees were not found.

permit_used: Carte de séjour / VLS-TS "Visiteur" (CESEDA L.426-20; passive income ≥ 12 × net SMIC per year)
digital_nomad_note: No special digital nomad visa was identified; not checked on official pages.
passive_income_note: Visiteur: an obligation not to engage in professional activity in France. Ministry of Interior (answer to written question № 11730 to the National Assembly, 23.06.2026): there is no normative text on remote work for a foreign economy; if the foreigner is not an employee in France and does not work for an enterprise located in France, remote work for an employer under foreign law "doit conduire à le considérer comme non-actif". This is a minister's answer, not a norm of law; the tax administration, per the text of the question, interprets it differently (work physically in France = work in France). Income must be confirmed by stable receipts (12 × net SMIC); remote earnings as "resources" is a grey area.
self_employed_note: VLS-TS "Entrepreneur"/profession libérale: business registration in France, taxes and social contributions in France (not checked on official pages). For a freelancer with foreign clients the status under the law was not verified.
real_estate_note: No residence permit via real estate in France.
family_note: The sample adult has no French relatives.
student_note: Student residence permit: working hours not checked on official pages; remote work for a foreign employer not verified.
local_clients: Not allowed: "fournir des prestations à des clients français, ou travailler pour un employeur français, est interdit sans ambiguïté" (demarchesetrangers.fr, legal blog). The response of the Ministry of Interior also refers to the absence of work "au bénéfice d'une entreprise située sur le territoire".
registration_needed: Under Visiteur one cannot register a sole proprietorship (that would be professional activity in France). For a stay of >183 days — tax residency, worldwide income is declared (forms 2042/2047, per demarchesetrangers).
employer_risk: No official position on PE found (the Ministry of Interior reply is only about the immigration qualification 'non-actif').
penalty: The sanctions article was not found (legifrance L426-20 — 403, did not circumvent). Something else is officially confirmed: the answer of the Ministry of Interior (JO 23.06.2026, p.5748): «Il est interdit au détenteur de cette carte de séjour temporaire d'exercer en France une activité professionnelle soumise à autorisation»; the prefecture of Hautes-Pyrénées requires «Attestation sur l'honneur de n'exercer aucune activité professionnelle en France».
notes: IMPORTANT CLARIFICATION that is not in the record: in the same reply the Ministry of Interior said: «Un ressortissant étranger résidant en France mais ne remplissant pas ces critères, et qui reste rémunéré et s'acquitte de la fiscalité liée dans son pays d'origine, doit solliciter une carte de séjour temporaire mention «visiteur»». I.e. the ministry's position is favourable to remote work for a foreign employer provided that the person remains paid and pays taxes in the country of origin, and does not work for an enterprise on the territory of France. For the sample adult: (1) the sample adult is not an employee but works for foreign clients — this exact case ("employeur de droit étranger") is not addressed in the reply for the self-employed; with a stay of >183 days tax residency arises in France (per a law blog), which contradicts the ministry's condition; (3) resources of 12 × net SMIC for Visiteur must be stable (prefecture) — income from work as a resource is disputed. The minister's reply is not a norm of law.
conditional_class_note: Visiteur: per the French Ministry of Interior reply of 23.06.2026, remote work for a foreign employer without clients in France is permitted; the case of a self-employed person is not directly addressed in the reply.

permit_used: Long-term visa (then long-term residence permit) for the purpose of business, for a self-employed person with a Czech trade licence (živnostenské oprávnění); or, for IT and marketing specialists from 12 listed countries, a long-term visa/permit for the purpose "other" (employee of a foreign company) or for business (freelancer) under the Digital Nomad Programme of the Ministry of Industry and Trade (CzechInvest)
digital_nomad_note: Digital Nomad Programme (Ministry of Industry and Trade, presented by CzechInvest): for people who work remotely as IT or marketing specialists and are citizens of Australia, Brazil, Canada, Israel, Japan, Mexico, New Zealand, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, the United Kingdom or the United States (CzechInvest). Two routes: an employee of a foreign company who stays employed abroad and has no Czech employment (long-term visa for the purpose "other"), or a freelancer who holds or will hold a Czech trade licence (long-term visa for the purpose of business). The ministry assesses applications, "there is no legal entitlement to participation in the Program"; the long-term visa/permit application is processed within 45 days (MZV Chicago, page of 18.09.2024). The official pages do not state an income threshold, insurance or tax terms; Fragomen (law firm, 24.02.2025) cites income of at least 1.5 times the average gross annual salary and a foreign employer with at least 50 employees worldwide, not confirmed on an official page.
self_employed_note: Long-term visa for the purpose of business: open to third-country nationals, the official pages list no nationalities; supporting documents include a trade licence extract or a company register extract, accommodation and proof of funds (no amount stated); the visa is valid for a maximum of 1 year and can be extended or changed to a long-term residence permit (MZV). Long-term residence permit for business: initial permit up to 2 years, extensions of up to 2 years, fee CZK 2,500, processing 60 days, comprehensive health insurance and proof of income required, no minimum amount stated (Ministry of the Interior portal ipc.gov.cz). A third-country national needs a residence permit to run a trade, but the trade can be notified first and the preliminary extract attached to the residence permit application (Brno city hall).
family_note: Digital Nomad Programme: the spouse, registered partner and child of the applicant (or of the spouse or partner) can apply for a long-term visa for the purpose of family at the same time (MZV Chicago, CzechInvest).
student_note: The right to work remotely on a student residence permit was not checked on an official page.
local_clients: Not clarified on the official pages: CzechInvest does not say whether clients must be foreign; for the employee route it excludes Czech employment ("does not enter into an employment relationship in the Czech Republic"). Fragomen (law firm, 24.02.2025): freelancers may do contract work for Czech entities; not confirmed on an official page.
registration_needed: Trade licence: a third-country national notifies the trade licensing office (fee CZK 1,000) and presents the residence permit within six months of the preliminary extract; registration with social security within 15 days and with a health insurer within 8 days of starting the activity (Brno city hall). Tax registration and tax terms of the employee route are not addressed on the official pages: not clarified.
employer_risk: Not clarified: the official pages do not address permanent-establishment or tax risk for a foreign employer of a remote worker in Czechia.
penalty: Not clarified: the official pages reviewed do not state sanctions for working without the proper permit.
notes: Re-checked 22.10.2026 on official pages: CzechInvest (Digital Nomad Programme), Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs (long-term visa for business; programme page of the consulate in Chicago), Ministry of the Interior portal ipc.gov.cz (long-term residence permit for business) and Brno city hall (trade licence for third-country nationals). Only the Chicago consulate page carries dates (published 18.09.2024, updated 11.10.2024); the list of 12 nationalities is as shown on the CzechInvest page on 22.10.2026. Classification: conditional, works in practice with a note — the trade-licence route is open to third-country nationals in general, the programme only to the listed nationalities and occupations. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).

permit_used: Permit without gainful employment (for example family reunification or education, or Art. 28 FNIA for retired persons), under which the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) classifies home-office work for a foreign employer with no Swiss establishment and no effect on the Swiss labour market (SEM circular of 5 April 2022). No dedicated remote-work or digital nomad permit
digital_nomad_note: No remote-worker permit category exists: the SEM circular states that a person who works from Switzerland for a foreign employer without a Swiss establishment and without effect on the Swiss labour market is to be admitted only under a permit without gainful employment (family reunification, education) (SEM circular, section 3). The SEM pages on working in Switzerland mention no digital nomad permit.
passive_income_note: Art. 28 FNIA (Retired persons): foreign nationals no longer gainfully employed may be admitted if they have reached a minimum age set by the Federal Council, have special personal relations to Switzerland and have the required financial means (Federal Act on Foreign Nationals and Integration, text as published on lawbrary.ch). The age threshold and the amount of means were not found on an official page.
self_employed_note: Gainful employment includes any salaried or self-employed activity normally carried out for payment and needs a permit irrespective of the period of stay (FNIA Art. 11). Admission of third-country nationals is tied to being highly qualified, to the economic interest and to quotas (SEM, Working in Switzerland: third-country nationals); the self-employment articles were not opened.
family_note: A permit for family reunification is named by SEM as a permit without gainful employment under which home-office work for a foreign employer without effect on the Swiss labour market is classified; holders of a permit for gainful employment or family reunification may do home-office work with Swiss market impact without a new permit (SEM circular, section 3a).
student_note: SEM names education and training permits among permits without gainful employment under which home-office work for a foreign employer without effect on the Swiss labour market is classified (SEM circular, section 3). Hours of permitted student work were not checked on an official page.
local_clients: Not permitted under a permit without gainful employment: home-office work that affects the Swiss labour market is always gainful employment subject to a permit, whatever its duration (SEM circular, section 3); for EU/EFTA nationals SEM adds that work for Swiss clients or customer acquisition in Switzerland excludes non-gainful status.
registration_needed: Applicants register with the local authorities within 14 days of entering Switzerland (SEM, Working in Switzerland). Social security: home-office work may shift the applicable social security law to the country of residence if the home-office share is substantial, with 25% of work or pay named as the threshold; the circular states that immigration, social security and tax definitions differ (SEM circular, section 4, April 2022). Tax follows the double taxation agreements: not clarified for individual cases.
employer_risk: Not clarified on permanent establishment. The SEM circular (April 2022) states that a change of social security regime can follow when the home-office share is substantial (25% of work or pay); permanent-establishment risk is not addressed in the circular.
penalty: Not clarified: the penalty provision of FNIA (Art. 115, unlawful gainful employment) was not opened on an official page.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: SEM (Working in Switzerland; third-country nationals), SEM circular 'Taetigkeit im Home Office; auslaenderrechtliche Qualifikation; FZA und Drittstaaten' of 5 April 2022 (addressed to cantonal authorities), FNIA Art. 11 and Art. 28 as published in bilingual and aggregator legal databases. Classification: conditional. Remote work for a foreign employer with no Swiss establishment and no effect on the Swiss labour market is not treated as a permit-requiring activity in the circular, but new admission is granted only under permits without gainful employment (family, education, retired persons); there is no permit built around remote work, and work with Swiss market impact needs a gainful-employment permit with quota and labour-market tests. The circular dates from April 2022 and is an internal SEM instruction. Not established: the official minimum age and financial threshold under Art. 28 FNIA, student work hours, Art. 115 penalties; the Fedlex consolidated text could not be opened (requires JavaScript) and ch.ch student page could not be fetched. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).
conditional_class_note: SEM classifies remote work for a foreign employer without Swiss market impact as possible only under a permit without gainful employment (family, education, retired persons), so it works for holders of such permits but no permit is issued for remote work as such.

permit_used: No permit for remote work for a foreign employer is described on the official pages opened.
