digital_nomad_note: No digital nomad or remote-work permission is listed among the permits on the Swedish Migration Agency pages for work, temporary work and visits (checked 2026-10-22); the absence from these lists is not a statement that remote work is prohibited.
self_employed_note: Swedish Migration Agency: "If you have your own business and are going to carry out temporary, remote work in Sweden, you do not need to apply for a work permit." The same page covers a business outside the EU with a temporary assignment on site: "If you have your own business outside the EU and have received a temporary assignment on site in Sweden, you do not need to apply for a work permit." A stay of more than 90 days needs a visitor's residence permit, with at least SEK 700 for each day of the visit; for a self-employed person the company's insurance is enough as medical travel insurance. The page does not define "temporary", and the conditions of the permit for settling in Sweden as self-employed were not opened.
family_note: not checked on official pages
student_note: right to work remotely on a student permit not checked on official pages
local_clients: Not clarified on the official pages opened: the page on temporary remote work by a self-employed person does not say whether clients must be outside Sweden.
registration_needed: Not clarified on the official pages opened: tax registration (Skatteverket) and business registration were not opened.
employer_risk: Not clarified: the pages of the Swedish Migration Agency do not address permanent-establishment or tax risk for a foreign employer of a remote worker in Sweden.
penalty: Not clarified: the pages opened do not state sanctions for working without a permit.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on the pages of the Swedish Migration Agency (migrationsverket.se: work, exemptions from the work permit requirement, temporary work in Sweden, self-employed with a temporary assignment, visitor's residence permit for more than 90 days), without regard to citizenship. Classification: unknown. A verdict of no needs an official norm or quotation that bans remote work for a foreign employer, and none was found; the first-pass verdict rested on an aggregator and on the absence of a nomad visa. What the official pages say: "In most cases, citizens of non-EU/EEA countries who want to work in Sweden need a work permit, but there are some exceptions." (exemptions page; the listed occupational groups do not include remote workers). For a person with a business, "If you have your own business and are going to carry out temporary, remote work in Sweden, you do not need to apply for a work permit." (self-employed page). For a stay of more than 90 days the visitor's residence permit requires "Your stay in Sweden must only be for the purpose of visiting the country" and "You must intend to leave Sweden after your stay"; the tourist category "does not give you the right to work" (visitor page, the sentence is cut off in the page structure). So the pages leave open whether a person living in Sweden on a residence permit may work remotely for a foreign employer; the page on temporary remote work by a self-employed person is the only direct statement. Not opened: Skatteverket (tax residence, tax on foreign employment income), regeringen.se, the Aliens Act, the permits for employees and for self-employed settling in Sweden. Web fetch was rate-limited during the check, the pages above were read in a browser. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).

permit_used: Digital nomad visa: Estonian short-stay (C, up to 90 days) or long-stay (D, up to 365 days) visa issued for the purpose of teleworking; a temporary stay, not a residence permit
digital_nomad_note: The visa is for people who can work location-independently and are (1) employed under a contract by an employer registered abroad, (2) partner or shareholder in a company registered abroad, or (3) freelancers or consultants mainly serving clients with foreign establishments under contracts (e-Residency FAQ, 11 March 2026). The application needs proof of legal income for six months, a written explanation of the teleworking purpose, an employer confirmation that the duties can be done remotely, a contract and health insurance covering the stay (Police and Border Guard Board). Income threshold: the e-Residency FAQ (11 March 2026) gives EUR 4,500 per month gross (benchmark EUR 150 per day); the Ministry of Foreign Affairs table for the category 'Teleworking (digital nomad visa)' gives EUR 132 per day (EUR 3,960 per month) and none for a spouse or minor children; the two official pages differ and the current figure should be confirmed with the consulate. State fee EUR 120 for the D visa, processing usually up to 30 days (Work in Estonia). The visa cannot be extended; a second visa can be applied for, total stay is limited to 548 days within 730 days (e-Residency FAQ). Restrictions on accepting applications apply to citizens of some states and to some places of application (Work in Estonia, e-Residency FAQ): availability depends on nationality and where the application is lodged.
self_employed_note: Freelancers and consultants are covered only if they mainly serve clients with foreign establishments under contracts, and partners or shareholders only for business activity for a company registered abroad (e-Residency FAQ). A residence permit for own business in Estonia was not checked on official pages.
family_note: A spouse and minor children may apply for the visa on conditions matching the holder's; spousal visas are decided case by case; the spouse's right to work depends on the visa conditions (e-Residency FAQ). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs financial-means table shows no separate requirement for a spouse or minor children.
student_note: Not checked on official pages.
local_clients: Conditional: the holder may take additional work for an Estonian company or employer, but the main purpose of the stay must remain the remote work stated in the application; registration of short-term employment and payment of the average Estonian salary are not required for that additional work (e-Residency FAQ, 11 March 2026).
registration_needed: Staying more than 183 days in a consecutive 12-month period makes the holder an Estonian tax resident who must declare and pay tax in Estonia; other tax questions are referred to the Tax and Customs Board, whose pages were not opened (e-Residency FAQ). Health insurance covering treatment costs for the whole stay is required (Police and Border Guard Board). Business or social security registration duties for the visa holder are not stated on the official pages reviewed: not clarified.
employer_risk: Not clarified: the official pages reviewed do not address permanent-establishment or tax risk for a foreign employer of a visa holder working in Estonia.
penalty: Not clarified for the digital nomad visa itself. For employment in Estonia in general, the Police and Border Guard Board says employment of a foreigner must be registered in advance and longer work requires a residence permit; the Labour Inspectorate may fine failure to register posted workers up to 300 fine units for a natural person and up to EUR 32,000 for a legal person (Labour Inspectorate). The Aliens Act sanction provisions could not be opened.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: Work in Estonia (Enterprise Estonia), Ministry of Foreign Affairs (long-stay D visa page, financial-means table), Police and Border Guard Board (long-term visa and working in Estonia pages), e-Residency programme FAQ (11 March 2026), Labour Inspectorate. Classification: yes. An official page states that a visa for the purpose of teleworking exists, with three eligible categories that all require a foreign employer, foreign company or foreign clients; stay is capped at 365 days per visa and 548 days within 730 days, and the visa does not lead to residence or citizenship. Not established: the two official income figures differ (EUR 4,500 versus EUR 3,960 per month); the Police and Border Guard Board digital nomad page and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs digital nomad page could not be opened; the Aliens Act text (Riigi Teataja requires JavaScript) and Tax and Customs Board pages were not read; the list of states whose citizens face application restrictions was not opened. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).

permit_used: Designated Activities (Digital Nomad, international remote work): up to six months, no extension, no residence card, annual income of at least 10 million yen, nationals of countries on the visa-exemption list that also have a tax convention with Japan
digital_nomad_note: Immigration Services Agency (ISA) page: remote work from Japan using information and communication technology under an employment contract with a foreign organisation, or providing services or selling goods for a fee to persons located in a foreign country; stay of six months, no extension; annual income of at least 10 million yen at application (tax or income certificate from the country of work); private medical travel insurance covering death, injury and illness with medical compensation of at least 10 million yen; no residence card; limited to nationals of countries under the visa-exemption arrangements (Temporary Visitor) that also have a tax convention with Japan; after the six months the applicant must wait six months before reapplying (ISA). The Japanese embassy page for this status says the visa is generally single-entry, to be used within 3 months of issue, and that applications may be referred to Japan for up to 2 months (Embassy of Japan, Portland PDF).
self_employed_note: Startup Visa (Foreign Entrepreneur Startup Promotion Program, METI): Designated Activities (Public Notice No. 51), up to two years to prepare a business, with a plan confirmed by a certified local organisation; the business must reach assets of at least 30 million yen and employ one full-time resident employee within one year (METI). Business Manager status (ISA page opened in a Japanese-language version) covers running or managing a business and lists a business premises, a business plan and at least one full-time employee among the requirements; the capital figure was not shown on the page opened (ISA).
family_note: Digital Nomad status: a supported spouse or child can obtain a Designated Activities status limited to six months with no extension, with an insurance requirement as for the main applicant, and the nationality conditions apply to them (ISA). The Dependent status is for a spouse or child of holders of certain working and student statuses (ISA, Japanese-language page).
student_note: The official study-in-Japan portal states that the student status does not permit work, and that part-time work is possible only after permission to engage in activities other than that permitted (Study in Japan). Remote work for a foreign employer on a student status is not addressed on the pages opened.
local_clients: No under the Digital Nomad status: employment under a contract with a Japanese public or private organisation is not permitted, and permitted services and sales are those directed to persons located in a foreign country (ISA). Whether other statuses allow Japanese clients was not checked.
registration_needed: Not clarified on the official pages: no residence card is issued for the Digital Nomad status, and the ISA page does not describe resident registration, tax or social security duties; the income certificate must come from the country where the applicant worked (ISA).
employer_risk: Not clarified: the official pages do not address permanent-establishment or tax risk for a foreign employer of a remote worker in Japan; the nomad status requires an employment contract with a foreign organisation and excludes Japanese employers (ISA).
penalty: Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act, Article 19(1): a person in a status listed in Appended Table I "shall not engage in" activities outside that status unless permitted; Article 24(iv)(a) makes a person engaged solely in such activities deportable (official English translation). Penalties under Article 70(1)(iv) (up to 3 years of imprisonment or a fine of up to 3 million yen) and Article 73 (up to 1 year or a fine of up to 2 million yen) are cited by an administrative scrivener firm; the penalty chapter could not be read in the official translation retrieved, so these figures are not confirmed on an official page.
notes: Re-checked 2026-10-22 on official pages: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (Designated Activities for Digital Nomad, PDF version of that page, Business Manager), Embassy of Japan in the United States (Digital Nomad visa PDF, Temporary Visitor page), METI (Startup Visa), JETRO (statuses of residence), Study in Japan portal and the official English translation of the Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act. Classification: conditional, works with a stated caveat. Japan has an official remote-work status that expressly allows work for a foreign employer or foreign clients, but only for six months without extension, with income of at least 10 million yen and for nationals of a list of eligible countries (visa-exempt and with a tax convention); the rule depends on nationality. Temporary visitors may not work: "the temporary visitor visa excludes profit-making operations and paid activities" (Embassy of Japan, Honolulu) and "Holders of temporary visitor status may not engage in working activities" (JETRO); the pages do not say how remote work for a foreign employer is treated on that status outside the nomad scheme. Not opened or not established: the list of eligible countries (separate ISA chart), English version of the Business Manager page, the penalty articles in the official translation, tax and social security terms. The row has not been through the separate verification pass (verified = false).
